title: Auxiliary Clues Aware’s Geometry Problem Solving
claim: A reinforcement learning loop reweights sequence-level advantages by token-level dependency on hidden auxiliary inputs, teaching transferable construction strategies.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right with feedback loop; colored module blocks, math under arrows
description: A single wide diagram with pastel-colored rounded modules connected by thick arrows. Bottom left, a gray Input box holds the question text q and two geometry diagrams, I_aux with auxiliary lines and I_org without. An arrow feeds the policy model (a logo icon) in the blue Rollout block, which outputs sampled sequences {y1..yG} shown as token chains t1..tT. At top center, a light-blue Compute ACD block runs two forward passes, conditioned on I_aux and I_org. Each pass gives a probability histogram, P_aux or P_org, and the two are subtracted to give the token-level dependency d_i. At bottom center, a green Compute Reward block has a reward model icon and Accuracy, Aux Usage and Format boxes, summed into r_i. At right, a gray AuxCA column applies φ to d_i, multiplies the result with the advantage A_i, and a gray arrow loops back to the policy model.
caption: The overall framework of AuxCA. Following GRPO, the policy model first samples a group of outputs {y1, · · · , yG} conditioned on the auxiliary-enhanced input Iaux. We then calculate the token-level Auxiliary Clues Dependency di by measuring the probability shift between predictions conditioned on Iaux and those conditioned on Iorg without auxiliary visual clues. The sampled sequences are then scored by the reward model to derive the sequence-level advantages Ai. Finally, the model parameters are optimized by adjusting the advantage Ai based on the dependency di via the function ψ, thereby helping the model learn transferable auxiliary-construction strategies.
abstract: Geometry Problem Solving (GPS) serves as a rigorous test of the complex reasoning capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly when solutions require auxiliary constructions absent from the input diagram. However, explicit diagramming methods suffer from unstable image generation quality and cascading errors, while existing implicit attention mechanisms primarily focus on visible elements, limiting their ability to support reasoning that requires additional geometric constructions. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{AuxCA} (Auxiliary-Clues-Aware GRPO), a reinforcement learning framework that helps models learn transferable auxiliary-construction strategies that can be applied beyond the training domain without explicit diagram generation at inference time. Specifically, we introduce Auxiliary Clues Dependency (\textbf{ACD}) to quantify the influence of auxiliary visual clues on token generation and integrate it into GRPO through fine-grained advantage weighting. Furthermore, we incorporate an auxiliary incentive reward to encourage the effective use of auxiliary geometric clues in correct solutions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AuxCA-8B outperforms the explicit-plotting baseline Bagel-Canvas and achieves competitive performance with leading proprietary models on auxiliary-dependent plane geometry problems. Improvements on analytic geometry, solid geometry, and external benchmarks further suggest that the learned strategies can transfer beyond the training domain. Code is available at https://github.com/fukua23/AuxCA
